chapter: Reel 4: boyhood bands and the drummers he admired
title: Big Sid Catlett: first meeting in Miami in 1935 and fishing at Wildwood
summary: Sid Catlett, with Don Redman's band, spent an intermission teaching him; later they hung out in California and fished at Wildwood.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah, he was an actor, but he also was a trombone player, and so he had a group, and I played with them up there for 10 years. It was Conrad, Dick Welston, the piano player, there was Eugene Sedrick, formerly with Fats Waller, was a clarinet player, and Herman Archer, also from the Fats Waller group was the another trumpet player -- and the first time I met Big Sid Catlett was in Miami in 1935; he came there with Don Redman, and in that band was Denny Morton, Quentin Jackson was the other trombone player, and Gene Simon. There were three trombones -- Gene Simon, Denny Morton and Quintin Jackson, who we called "Brutta".

And that was the first time I had ever seen a trombone with a great big bell on it. I don't know where Denny Morton got this trombone from, but it had an extra large bell on it, you know? And it really was impressive to me.
And the piano player was a guy named Kirk-Kilpatrick, who was also a great arranger at that time around Miami.
Who was the drummer in that band?
Yeah, that's my first time seeing him. And he spent his whole intermission talking to me, and I was very much impressed with him.
Well, [he'd ask me] different things about the drums, and he was trying to play -- and things I would see him do, I would ask about them, and he tried to explain them to me.

And, later on, when I came to New York, whenever he was in town, we used to hang out together every now and then, and I will never forget the time that I was out in California, and he had his own group at a club there, I think the club was called The Last Word, that was where I first saw Allen Eager -- Allen Eager was playing out there at the time.

And Sid and I used to hang out there, because at that time, he was doing very well for himself; I mean, as a leader. Then I got the pleasure of being with him again in at Wildwood, New Jersey when he was with Louis Armstrong. Louis Armstrong had Jack Teagarden T. Garden and Aurell Shore, and Earl Hines Arvell Shaw,
Yeah, I think I was working there with you with Cab Calloway.
We were with Cab Calloway; we also played there, too, in Wildwood.

Well, Big Sid and I went fishing one day while we were there, and we both got sea sick as soon as we got out into the ocean there, and we were sick for quite awhile, but we were fortunate enough that we just pulled ourselves together and we went out there and fished, and I think that between the two of us, we caught enough fish that we had a fishfry that night after work, and everybody just had a good time on that fish... And Louis was there ...
Yeah, I remember that, man. I remember that quite well.
